subject: design-technology

moments.title: Arkwright's water frame patent
moments.body:
Arkwright patents a water-powered spinning frame and builds factory accommodation for workers.

The factory system reorganises labour around the machine, not the household.
moments.takeaway: Design choices about machinery rewrote how communities lived.

moments.title: Great Exhibition, Crystal Palace
moments.body:
Joseph Paxton's Crystal Palace, fabricated from cast iron and glass, hosts six million visitors.

The exhibition consolidates Britain's design and manufacturing leadership while sparking critique of mass-produced ornament.
moments.takeaway: Trade exhibitions became both showcases and battlegrounds for design philosophy.

moments.title: Morris & Co. founded
moments.body:
The firm produces wallpaper, textiles and furniture in conscious reaction to industrial ornament.

Morris's Arts and Crafts ideals will face the contradiction that hand-made goods are expensive.
moments.takeaway: The first systematic design ideology positioned itself against mass production.

now.title: Industrial design today
now.body: Industry 4.0, additive manufacturing and globalised supply chains create new design constraints. End-of-life and circular-economy thinking reframe what 'good design' means.
now.open_questions: Can mass production align with circular flows? What is the role of national manufacturing in resilience?

reflection: The economic possibilities of industrialisation and the social costs were debated by designers from the start.
